It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. div.head: Quadr Ded 28
div.ab: Nec iam uereor indignantis animi turbidis seditionibus Eusebio sociari sub opere multiplici, quod intendit omnibus penam uitiis, pretium uirtutibus, et tanto difficiliores consummatæ diligentiæ reddit accessus, quanto prauis cupiditatibus fomentisque disparibus rerum ueritas oppugnatur, quot negotiis, tot sententiis et errore dubiis altercationibus infirmata.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 531 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Anspielung auf De operibus bonis et malis unter den Scripta dubia des Eusebius von Caesarea?
An allusion to De operibus bonis et malis among the Scripta dubia of Eusebius of Caesarea?

div.ab: Nor do I now fear, with the turbulent seditions of an indignant mind, to be associated with Eusebius in a manifold work, which aims at punishment for all vices, reward for virtues, and makes the approaches to completed diligence the more difficult, the more the truth of things is assailed by depraved desires and unequal incitements, weakened by as many opinions as there are affairs and by doubtful disputes in error.
